```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 3.5)
suppressPackageStartupMessages(pkgload::load_all("..", quiet = TRUE, export_all = FALSE))
library(ggplot2)
a <- analyse(params$data)
pct <- function(x, digits = 1) sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f%%"), 100 * x)
palette <- c(desktop = "#9aa5b1", mobile = "#d64545")
```

Every number below is computed by the `funnellens` R package from the raw export `r a$dataset$export`
(`r a$dataset$period_start` to `r a$dataset$period_end`, a 1-in-`r round(1 / a$dataset$sample_rate)` sample).
Knitting this file from a clean checkout reproduces it exactly; CI does that with `make report`.
The formulas are in `contract/questions.md`.

## Q1 · Can we trust the export?

```{r quality}
issues <- data.frame(issue = names(a$data_quality$issues), rows = unlist(a$data_quality$issues))
knitr::kable(issues, row.names = FALSE)
checks <- do.call(rbind, lapply(a$data_quality$checks, function(c) {
  data.frame(id = c$id, severity = c$severity, status = c$status, failing_rows = c$failing_rows)
}))
knitr::kable(checks)
```

## Q2 · The funnel by device

```{r funnel}
rates <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("desktop", "mobile"), function(d) {
  r <- a$funnel$by_device[[d]]$step_rates
  data.frame(device = d, step = factor(names(r), levels = names(r)), rate = unlist(r))
}))
ggplot(rates, aes(step, rate, fill = device)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = palette) +
  labs(title = "Mobile falls behind at the cart and payment steps", y = "share of the previous step")
```

Mobile is `r pct(a$funnel$mobile_share_of_sessions)` of sessions but `r pct(a$funnel$mobile_share_of_revenue)` of revenue.

## Q3 · Is the mobile payment step worse?

```{r payment}
p <- a$payment_step_test
```

Mobile `r pct(p$mobile$rate)` vs desktop `r pct(p$desktop$rate)` of checkouts become purchases:
`r sprintf("%+.1f", 100 * p$difference)` pp, 95 % CI [`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * p$ci95[1])`,
`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * p$ci95[2])`] pp, z = `r sprintf("%.2f", p$z)`, p = `r format(p$p_value, digits = 2)`.

## Q4 · Compare like with like: within each acquisition channel

```{r channels}
ch <- do.call(rbind, lapply(a$by_channel$channels, function(c) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(c("desktop", "mobile"), function(d) {
    n <- c[[d]]$checkout
    data.frame(channel = c$channel, device = d, checkouts = n, pay_rate = if (n > 0) c[[d]]$purchase / n else NA)
  }))
}))
ggplot(ch, aes(channel, pay_rate, fill = device)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = palette) +
  labs(title = "Within every channel, mobile pays less often after checkout", y = "purchase / checkout")
cmh <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(a$by_channel$cmh), function(s) {
  t <- a$by_channel$cmh[[s]]
  data.frame(step = s, odds_ratio_mh = t$odds_ratio_mh, ci_low = t$ci95[1], ci_high = t$ci95[2],
             p_value = t$p_value, crude = t$crude_odds_ratio)
}))
knitr::kable(cmh, digits = 4)
```

## Q5 · Do mobile buyers spend less?

```{r value}
v <- a$order_value
```

Mobile ₹`r format(round(v$mobile$mean_inr), big.mark = ",")` vs desktop
₹`r format(round(v$desktop$mean_inr), big.mark = ",")` per order: Welch t = `r sprintf("%.2f", v$welch_t)`,
df = `r round(v$df)`, p = `r sprintf("%.2f", v$p_value)`.

## Q6 · Is the weekly trend stable?

```{r weekly}
w <- do.call(rbind, lapply(a$weekly, function(r) {
  data.frame(week = r$week, device = c("desktop", "mobile"),
             conversion = c(r$conversion$desktop, r$conversion$mobile))
}))
ggplot(w, aes(week, conversion, colour = device, group = device)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = palette) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5)) +
  labs(title = "Conversion per ISO week: no break or backfill")
```

## Q7 · What is the gap worth?

```{r opportunity}
o <- a$opportunity
```

If mobile paid like desktop within each channel: ₹`r sprintf("%.1f", o$monthly_revenue_uplift_inr / 1e5)` lakh per
month (`r pct(o$uplift_share_of_mobile_revenue)` of mobile revenue).

## Q8 · Recommendation

**`r a$decision$recommendation`** because `r paste(a$decision$reasons, collapse = ", ")`.

**Caveats.** Observational data: channel is the confounder we can see, not the only one. The uplift assumes
mobile could reach desktop's within-channel payment rate, which only an experiment can show.
